name: workflowers-events-to-scw-busy

deploy.description: One half of the two-way calendar-blocking pair (with scw-events-to-workflowers-block; gcal-block-sweep is the shared horizon backstop). Mirrors every timed, busy, non-declined event on the dennis@work.flowers Google Calendar onto dchiuten@securecodewarrior.com as a PRIVATE, BARE 'Busy' block — no title, description, location or attendees leak into the SCW workspace. Keyed through the GCal Sync Map table so updates move the block and cancellations delete it. Refuses to create a mirror for an occurrence starting more than 60 days out; the sweep fills those in as they approach. Replaces Notion Calendar's built-in event blocking, which SCW IT cut off on 2026-08-28.

trigger.authentication_note: work.flowers Google Calendar connection ('Google Calendar dennis@work.flowers') — the calendar being READ. Same id gcal-event-updated-to-meeting-note carries on its trigger; that Zap and this one both poll dennis@work.flowers and coexist fine. The SCW credential is a --connections alias because the workflow writes there.
trigger.trigger_note: Polling trigger, fires on create AND update. Cancellations arrive through it too as sparse status:'cancelled' tombstones (observed on gcal-event-updated-to-meeting-note's production runs) — verify on the first real cancellation after cutover; the fallback is a second deployment on event_cancelled.
trigger.params_note: expand_recurring: true DELIBERATELY differs from gcal-event-updated-to-meeting-note (false): blocking needs one mirror per occurrence, keyed on the occurrence id. The workflow's 60-day horizon guard bounds the resulting volume (a weekly series expands ~730 instances in one poll).

connections_note: gcal_scw is the SCW Google Calendar connection 'dchiuten@securecodewarrior.com' (created 2026-08-28) — the DESTINATION this workflow creates/moves/deletes bare Busy blocks on.

tables.01M13QPJ5GRJV33096MBNSN1Q5: GCal Sync Map — source occurrence id -> mirror event id, both directions. SHARED with scw-events-to-workflowers-block and gcal-block-sweep: loop guard, update/delete target map, change detector. Columns: Source Event ID (f1), Mirror Event ID (f2), Direction (f3), Status (f4), Start (f5), End (f6), Summary (f7 — the SOURCE title, for debugging; the mirror itself is always 'Busy'), Source Updated (f8).
